data.title: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to boost sentiment in the AI ​​sector on its first day of trading.
data.description:
Author: Xiao Yanyan, Jinshi Data

Artificial intelligence company Anthropic delivered a stellar performance on its first day of trading, but this record-breaking IPO has also brought the opportunities and risks facing the entire AI industry into the spotlight.

On Thursday, Anthropic officially began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. The stock price initially surged after opening, then retreated somewhat, ultimately closing at $97.17, a 17% increase from its IPO price of $83.. Based on fully diluted share capital, the company's market capitalization is approximately $1.8 trillion, placing it among the top 10 most valuable publicly traded companies globally.

This IPO raised $81.3 billion, surpassing the record-breaking IPO size of SpaceX (SPCX) in June of this year.

In addition, Anthropic raised $26 billion through a concurrent private placement, bringing its total financing to $107.3 billion. This IPO came at a time of several weeks of volatility in the US stock market. The departure of Jensen Huang, the long-time CEO of Nvidia (NVDA), exacerbated investor concerns about the AI ​​industry's financing system; the Democratic Party's victory in the midterm elections also prompted the market to assess future changes in AI regulation and data center construction policies. On Thursday, the overall technology stock market continued to be under pressure. The S&P 500 fell 2%, and the Nasdaq 100 fell 2.2%. Jordan Watson, Managing Director of Investments at Tandem Investment Advisors, stated, “You can see that market sentiment surrounding AI has been deteriorating, and this trend hasn’t stopped today. The most important thing for the market right now is that Anthropic has become the most transparent real-time indicator for observing AI risky trades.” [Image of Anthropic IPO subscription demand nearing 7 times its offering size, with tech giants participating in private placements] Despite weak market sentiment, Anthropic’s IPO subscription demand remained very strong. According to a previous Bloomberg report, the overall subscription demand for this IPO was nearly seven times the number of shares available for issuance. At that time, the company still had two days before the subscription period ended and the official roadshow began. Ultimately, Anthropic set the offering price above the original range, and further expanded the offering size. This private placement attracted major players in the AI ​​industry, including Nvidia, Alphabet (GOOGL and GOOG), Microsoft (MSFT), and AMD. This reflects the increasingly close capital ties between companies across the AI ​​industry chain. However, competition among institutional investors was equally fierce. According to sources, more than half of the institutional investors who participated in the bidding ultimately failed to obtain any shares. Retail investors, on the other hand, obtained approximately 15% of the available shares. Because the relevant placement information has not yet been made public, the sources requested anonymity. An Anthropic spokesperson declined to comment. This IPO further gives Anthropic a competitive edge over its rival OpenAI, which currently has no plans to go public before 2027. Anthropic has also established a significant strategic partnership with Nvidia, committing to invest tens of billions of dollars through related agreements to secure access to Nvidia's most advanced chips. However, this model of companies investing in, financing, and purchasing each other's products has also raised concerns about "circular financing" in the AI ​​industry. Investors are beginning to examine whether providing financial support to AI clients by tech giants could contribute to financing and valuation bubbles. Rapid revenue growth, but huge computing power costs test profitability. Anthropic was founded nearly six years ago by a group of former OpenAI executives. A key reason the founding team left OpenAI was their desire to prioritize AI safety in technology development. The company employs a Public Benefit Corporation structure, balancing shareholder interests with social benefits, and has established a Long-Term Benefit Trust. This trust has the power to elect and remove a majority of the company's board members. Emphasizing AI safety has not prevented Anthropic from rapidly expanding its business. With its enterprise-facing business model, the company has seen significant revenue growth, particularly with the widespread adoption of the Claude Code programmable intelligence. Regulatory filings show that as of October 31, Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion, an increase of $10 billion from the end of September. Annualized revenue run rate is an extrapolation of full-year revenue based on revenue performance over a shorter period. The number of customers is also growing rapidly. As of the end of September, Anthropic had over 11,900 customers contributing at least $100,000 in revenue over the past 12 months, and this number is projected to reach approximately 1,500 by 2025. Claude Code has already been adopted by users including engineers at NASA. Anthropic also plans to expand its business into more professional fields such as law and healthcare. Novartis AG CEO Vas Narasimhan is also a member of Anthropic's board of directors. Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Mandeep Singh and William Tong believe that the increased IPO size and pricing reflect market optimism about the potential of Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) technology. This type of technology is expected to help AI companies further optimize computing costs and expand into new markets such as drug discovery. Both analysts pointed out that Anthropic's self-developed intelligent agent products are a key factor in maintaining a high net income retention rate and resisting competition. The company faces competitors including tech giants like Google and Meta, whose cutting-edge models include Gemini and Muse. However, behind this rapid growth lies ever-expanding infrastructure spending. Anthropic recorded an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter. Of this, computing power costs under short-term commitments reached $5 billion, and non-cash expenses related to the company's charitable matching program reached $2 billion. Bloomberg News previously reported that Goldman Sachs research analysts expect Anthropic to achieve positive annual free cash flow only by 2030. Nevertheless, Goldman Sachs analysts still predict that the company's annual revenue could reach approximately $685 billion by 2030. To achieve this goal, Anthropic must also contend with pricing pressure from low-cost, open-weighted models, including those offered by Chinese developers. AI security and financing risks coexist; IPO tests the entire industry. Anthropic's IPO has once again brought AI security to the forefront of market attention. Regulators, investors, and even Anthropic employees have warned of the potential loss of control over artificial intelligence. One individual believes there is a greater than 10% probability that AI could cause the extinction of humanity within the next decade. Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has also warned that the powerful capabilities of AI could trigger an event that could kill "one billion people." Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has been a leading figure advocating for top AI labs to slow down the development of cutting-edge technologies and prioritize safety. Meanwhile, leadership changes at Nvidia, financing arrangements for AI companies, and the Democratic Party's victory in the midterm elections have led investors to reassess the risks across the industry. Market concerns include potential increased regulatory scrutiny of AI safety and stricter restrictions on data center construction by various states. The sustainability of AI infrastructure investment and the ability of financing and guarantee arrangements between tech companies to generate genuine commercial returns have become critical issues affecting industry valuations. Gina Martin Adams, Chief Market Strategist at HB Wealth, stated that Thursday's market weakness continued the trend of the past few weeks, with significant investor concerns about the semiconductor industry and financing issues in the AI ​​ecosystem dragging down the entire market. She also pointed out that some market sell-offs may be related to investors selling other stocks to free up funds to buy Anthropic. A record IPO drives record-breaking US IPO fundraising for the year. Anthropic's listing further boosted the fundraising size of the US IPO market this year. Bloomberg data shows that, as of Wednesday, including Anthropic's listing, total US IPO fundraising in 2026 will approach $246 billion, surpassing the record of $195 billion set in 2021. This statistic does not include financial instruments such as blank check companies. This year's fundraising was largely driven by SpaceX's listing. SpaceX highlighted market opportunities in the AI ​​field as one of its key selling points during its IPO presentation. In addition, South Korean memory chip manufacturer SK Hynix further expanded its total financing by issuing $26.5 billion in American Depositary Receipts (ADRs). Anthropic's listing will also bring subsequent stock supply. According to company filings, in addition to the 980 million shares issued in the IPO, non-founding employees, board members, and former employees can sell up to 315 million shares on the first day of trading, including shares held by Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao. Approximately 15.5 billion shares held by insiders are subject to lock-up agreements, which will remain in effect until after the company's third-quarter results are released next year. Meanwhile, Anthropic may also benefit from passive buying demand from index funds. If it meets the criteria for early inclusion in indices, the company could be included in the Russell 1000 and Nasdaq 100 indices as early as December this year. This year, both FTSE Russell and Nasdaq adjusted their rules to expedite the inclusion of large newly listed companies in their indices. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley served as lead underwriters for this IPO, with 20 other banks participating. The shares are traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Anthropic's strong performance on its first day of trading demonstrates the continued huge demand in the capital markets for cutting-edge AI companies. However, as the company's financing scale, revenue, and computing power expenditure expand simultaneously, investors will need to focus not only on how much commercial value AI technology can create, but also on whether these companies can translate rapid growth into sustainable profits and cash flow.
